$comment: Cross-runtime vectors for the signed control-plane bootstrap envelope. Generated by scripts/generate-bootstrap-vectors.mjs from protocol/typescript/src/bootstrap/control-plane-bootstrap.ts. The keys are published test vectors, not credentials.

cases.name: accepted-primary-key
cases.why: The ordinary case: a signed prod envelope with an epoch above anything this client has seen.

cases.name: accepted-rotated-key
cases.why: Two keys are trusted at once so a rotation can be published before the old key is retired.

cases.name: accepted-no-relay
cases.why: A deployment with no managed relay omits relayOrigin; its absence is not a missing field.

cases.name: unknown-key
cases.why: A correctly signed envelope under a key no build trusts. Refused, and never a reason to go and fetch that key.

cases.name: bad-signature-tampered-database-url
cases.why: The endpoint edited after signing — the substitution the signature exists to stop.

cases.name: bad-signature-tampered-functions-url
cases.why: Same, on the other endpoint: every field is covered, not just the interesting-looking ones.

cases.name: bad-signature-tampered-project-id
cases.why: And on the project id, which is what actually decides whose data a client reads.

cases.name: wrong-environment
cases.why: A validly signed QA payload offered to a prod build. One leaked key must not walk a prod install onto a test project.

cases.name: epoch-rollback
cases.why: A correctly signed OLD envelope replayed after a rotation. This is the attack, not an edge case.

cases.name: epoch-equal-is-not-newer
cases.why: Equal is not newer. Accepting it would let the same epoch be re-signed with different endpoints.

cases.name: not-yet-valid
cases.why: A notBefore in the future is REFUSED, not waited for: an envelope that is not valid yet is not a reason to stop using the one that is.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-loopback
cases.why: A prod client pointed at localhost. The quietest possible redirection, and the one a signature alone would allow.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-private-range
cases.why: And at a private address, which is the same move from another machine on the network.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-bracketed-ipv6-loopback
cases.why: IPv6 arrives bracketed, so a host parsed with split(":")[0] is "[" and the loopback check never fires. The spelling that gets this wrong in every language.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-ipv4-mapped-ipv6
cases.why: And the IPv4-mapped spelling of the same address.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-plain-http
cases.why: Plain HTTP in prod: the endpoints are authenticated, and the transport must be too.

cases.name: emulator-endpoint-allowed-in-local
cases.why: A local build MAY point at an emulator: that is what a local build is for. The rule is `local`-only, and deliberately so — dev, qa and prod all talk to real servers.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-refused-in-dev
cases.why: The same emulator endpoints stamped `dev`. `dev` means real servers; a loopback endpoint in a dev envelope is the redirection the rule exists to stop, not a convenience.

cases.name: insecure-endpoint-refused-in-qa
cases.why: And stamped `qa`: the shared tier is no closer to a laptop than prod is.

cases.name: accepted-local
cases.why: A local build accepts a validly signed local envelope.

cases.name: wrong-environment-local-offered-to-dev
cases.why: A validly signed local envelope offered to a dev build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-local-offered-to-qa
cases.why: A validly signed local envelope offered to a qa build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-local-offered-to-prod
cases.why: A validly signed local envelope offered to a prod build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: accepted-dev
cases.why: A dev build accepts a validly signed dev envelope.

cases.name: wrong-environment-dev-offered-to-local
cases.why: A validly signed dev envelope offered to a local build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-dev-offered-to-qa
cases.why: A validly signed dev envelope offered to a qa build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-dev-offered-to-prod
cases.why: A validly signed dev envelope offered to a prod build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: accepted-qa
cases.why: A qa build accepts a validly signed qa envelope.

cases.name: wrong-environment-qa-offered-to-local
cases.why: A validly signed qa envelope offered to a local build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-qa-offered-to-dev
cases.why: A validly signed qa envelope offered to a dev build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-qa-offered-to-prod
cases.why: A validly signed qa envelope offered to a prod build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: accepted-prod
cases.why: A prod build accepts a validly signed prod envelope.

cases.name: wrong-environment-prod-offered-to-local
cases.why: A validly signed prod envelope offered to a local build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-prod-offered-to-dev
cases.why: A validly signed prod envelope offered to a dev build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: wrong-environment-prod-offered-to-qa
cases.why: A validly signed prod envelope offered to a qa build. Refused on the environment, whatever the endpoints say.

cases.name: malformed-retired-environment-production
cases.why: The retired spelling `production` is not an alias of `prod`. A payload carrying it is malformed, and there is no build it could be offered to.

cases.name: malformed-retired-environment-staging
cases.why: Likewise `staging` for `qa`. No compatibility parser, no migration window: the vocabulary changed in one step from an empty state.

cases.name: unsupported-version
cases.why: A schemaVersion this build does not know is refused rather than partially read — half a client on the old project is the failure this avoids.

cases.name: malformed-missing-field
cases.why: A required endpoint absent. Malformed, not "use the old value for that one".

cases.name: malformed-billing-host-is-a-url
cases.why: A billing allowlist entry must be a HOSTNAME. A caller that could write `https://x/` or `*.example.com` here would be writing a matcher, and every matcher this project has needed has eventually matched something it should not.

cases.name: malformed-billing-host-uppercase
cases.why: Lower-cased, so a comparison never has to decide which case to fold. An entry that is not already lower-case is a document somebody hand-edited.

cases.name: malformed-wrong-container-version
cases.why: An envelope claiming a container version that does not exist.
